note: Behavior-trace evals. The console skill mutates a live tmux session (respawns panes, rewrites project scripts), so most are answered by an agent that READS the skill files and traces the flow — verifying the text produces the intended behavior unambiguously rather than executing against a real session. Evals 9-11 check routing between the two sibling skills (console = wiring and verification, decorate = visual vocabulary) from the user's opening prompt; eval 17 checks the harder case, where a console-framed task drifts into chrome mid-flow and must hand off rather than improvise. Routing is the main ambiguity risk in this plugin. Evals 12-16 are live: they execute the bundled scripts and assert on real output.

evals.prompt: I edited scripts/watch-orders to change the refresh interval but the pane still shows the old countdown. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that a tmux pane keeps executing the process it was launched with, so editing the file on disk cannot affect it. Prescribes the verify loop: sandbox render in a disposable session, then `tmux respawn-pane -k -t <pane_id>` with an absolute path, then `tmux capture-pane -e -p` to confirm — and explicitly rejects Ctrl-C + send-keys retype, because an interrupt mid-child-call is swallowed and the typed command lands as inert text.

evals.prompt: Add a pane to my tmuxp session that shows deploy status, refreshing every couple of minutes.
evals.expected_output: Reads/creates .tmuxp.yaml, picks a layout (main-vertical + main-pane-width for interactive-focus, main-horizontal for log-dominant), creates a `scripts/watch-<name>` wrapper that ends in `exec viddy -p --unfold -n <secs> -- <one-shot renderer>` rather than putting the command inline in the yaml, builds a one-shot renderer to the standard, and finishes with the sandbox → respawn → capture verify loop. Cadence matches data cadence (120s+ for slow-moving state).

evals.prompt: This pane script prints fine in my terminal but shows up with no colors inside tmux. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Attributes it to TTY auto-detection: a pane is not a TTY, so any library's isatty() check strips color silently. The renderer must always emit ANSI unless NO_COLOR is set. If a `watch` fallback is in play, notes that `-c` is required to keep ANSI. If an external tool (gum, glow, bat) is producing the output, reaches CLICOLOR_FORCE=1 — not FORCE_COLOR, which is the Node convention and does nothing for Go tools — or writes to #{pane_tty} so stdout is a real terminal.

evals.prompt: Make the output of this monitoring script a proper table instead of a wall of text.
evals.expected_output: Applies the table idiom: bold header, thin rule under it, two-space column gaps, right-aligned numerics, and DISPLAY-COLUMN width math via the kit's vlen()/pad() rather than len() or str.ljust. Reuses the project's existing renderer if one exists rather than duplicating its data loading; otherwise copies scripts/renderer_template.py from ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}. Sizes the table to the pane's real estate via `tmux display -p "#{pane_width}x#{pane_height}"`, then SUBTRACTS the refresh wrapper's own cut before sizing — that figure is the pane, not the content area (under viddy, 4 rows and the right-hand column). A wrapping table is worse than the raw text it replaced.

evals.prompt: Audit my tmux panes and tell me which ones need work.
evals.expected_output: Lists panes with `tmux list-panes -s -F "#{window_name} #{pane_id} #{pane_current_command}"`, captures each with `tmux capture-pane -e -p`, and flags: absent ANSI color, clear-loop wrappers, wall-of-text with no structure, raw tail/cat panes, non-local timestamps, flicker-prone full redraws, and viddy invoked without -w/--unfold (a sweep over scripts/watch-*, since copied wrappers share the omission). Reports a verdict table rendered to the standard, and stays read-only until asked to fix.

evals.prompt: viddy isn't installed on this box. How do I refresh the pane?
evals.expected_output: Checks `command -v viddy`, offers to install (brew install viddy / go install), and gives the ordered fallback: `watch -c -n <secs>` (with -c called out as what preserves ANSI), then `while :; do tput cup 0 0; <cmd>; tput ed; sleep <secs>; done`. Explicitly refuses a `clear` loop and explains why — the blank frame between redraws IS the flicker.

evals.prompt: My lnav pane parses the plain log lines but every field from the labeled format comes back NULL.
evals.expected_output: Consults references/lnav-formats.md. Diagnoses non-mutually-exclusive regexes: lnav takes the first pattern that matches rather than the most specific, so the general pattern eats the labeled lines. Fix is a negative lookahead guarding the general pattern, e.g. (?<body>(?![A-Z]{1,8}: ).*). Validates headlessly with `lnav -i` then `lnav -n -c ';SELECT …'`, noting the table is named after the format key and the fallback body column is log_body. Ends by respawning the lnav pane so the new format loads.

evals.prompt: My pane redraws but I keep catching it half-updated — the top half is the new frame and the bottom is the old one.
evals.expected_output: Identifies tearing rather than flicker, and prescribes synchronized output: wrap the whole frame in `printf '\033[?2026h'` … `printf '\033[?2026l'` so the emulator commits one complete frame. Notes tmux passes mode 2026 through from 3.7 onward and ignores it harmlessly before that, so it is safe to add unconditionally. Does NOT suggest a clear-loop or a sleep as the fix.

evals.prompt: My dashboard pane works fine but it's ugly — can you make it prettier?
evals.expected_output: Routes to the decorate skill, not console. Picks a theme (asking whether the terminal background is light or dark, since that cannot be detected), names semantic roles rather than raw color codes, and matches primitives to data shape — badge/kv for single values, bar for ratios, sparkline for series, table for rows. Hands off to console's verify loop at the end rather than restating it.

evals.prompt: Style my tmux status bar to match the colors my panes use, and put the git branch on the right.
evals.expected_output: Routes to decorate (chrome action). Uses scripts/tmux_theme.sh to generate a snippet to a separate file and instructs the user to `tmux source-file` it — explicitly does NOT rewrite ~/.tmux.conf in place. Sets terminal-features RGB or the hex colors get quantized. Raises status-left-length/status-right-length above their defaults of 10 and 40. For the branch, knows `#()` never blocks, is always one tick stale, uses only the last output line, and runs under /bin/sh. Verifies the result rather than assuming it: knows `display-message -a` shows what an option EXPANDS to, not what the client draws, and reaches for the nested read-only client capture (`tmux attach -r` into a correctly-sized probe session, `capture-pane -e`) to confirm the bar is not clipped at the real client width — keeping the `-r`, which is what stops the probe resizing the live session.

evals.prompt: The columns in my status table go crooked whenever a row contains an emoji or a Japanese product name.
evals.expected_output: Routes to decorate. Diagnoses display-column width: len() counts characters, not columns — CJK and most emoji are 2 columns, VS16 promotes a 1-column glyph to 2, and a ZWJ sequence is many code points but one 2-column glyph. Prescribes the kit's vlen()/pad(), notes that ANSI stripping must cover OSC-8 hyperlinks and not just SGR, and recommends keeping emoji out of interior table columns in favor of EAW=Neutral marks like ✓ ✗ ▸.

evals.prompt: Run the bundled renderer template's demo mode and confirm the output meets the standard.
evals.expected_output: `python3 scripts/renderer_template.py demo` exits 0 and emits real SGR escape sequences (not literal [38;5;…m text): a ▌-prefixed section title, a bold header row over a rule, right-aligned numeric columns padded correctly despite embedded color codes, ▰▱ gauges, a bar, a sparkline, a framed panel, and a dim ∅ empty-state line. The default palette is ansi256-legacy — note it is selected by TMUX_DESIGN_THEME, which tmux_theme.sh sets session-wide, so pass `--theme ansi256-legacy` explicitly to test the default deterministically. All seven original v0.1.0 codes (1;38;5;212, 1;38;5;117, 38;5;114, 38;5;203, 38;5;221, 1;38;5;208, 2) still appear; the newer badge and accent roles add sequences that did not exist in v0.1.0.

evals.prompt: Verify the renderer degrades correctly across color depths.
evals.expected_output: `demo --theme nord --depth truecolor` emits 38;2; sequences; `--depth 256` emits 38;5; and zero 38;2;; `--depth 16` emits neither. NO_COLOR=1 emits zero ESC bytes of any kind. Knows that the default ansi256-legacy theme stores explicit 256 indices, so it stays 38;5; at truecolor depth by design (byte-compatibility with v0.1.0) and degrades to the nearest basic color — not to no color — at depth 16. Understands NO_COLOR outranks FORCE_COLOR and CLICOLOR_FORCE, and that the renderer deliberately does not call isatty() because a pane is not a TTY.

evals.prompt: Prove the table renderer aligns rows that contain wide characters.
evals.expected_output: Renders a table whose rows include ⛔ (East Asian Width W, 2 columns), CJK text, a VS16 emoji, a regional-indicator flag pair, and a ZWJ sequence, then measures each rendered line with vlen() and asserts every row has identical display width. Verifies by measurement rather than by visual inspection, since a one-column error is invisible to the eye but breaks the column.

evals.prompt: Generate the tmux chrome for the nord theme and check it actually loads.
evals.expected_output: `scripts/tmux_theme.sh nord` writes to stdout only and never touches ~/.tmux.conf. Output loads via `tmux source-file` in a disposable, `-L`-isolated session (`tmux -L <sock> -f /dev/null new-session -d`) — NOT a `TMUX_TMPDIR` sandbox, which is ignored whenever `$TMUX` is already set and would land on the live server — with no error, and `tmux -L <sock> display-message -p '#{E:status-left}'` expands to real values. An unknown theme name exits non-zero with the list of valid names. Kills the sandbox server afterwards via the same `-L` socket, never a bare `kill-server`.

evals.prompt: Someone's branch name is displaying weirdly and reversing the rest of my status row.
evals.expected_output: Identifies a bidi control character (U+202A-202E or U+2066-2069) in the untrusted text: zero display columns but it visually reverses everything after it — a layout bug and a spoofing vector. Prescribes sanitize() before layout, which strips bidi controls and C0/C1 while deliberately preserving ZWJ so emoji still render as one glyph. Applies to any untrusted source: branch names, log lines, commit messages, filenames.

evals.prompt: Polish my `invest` tmux workspace to maximize the UX — the panes, the status bar, the borders, all of it.
evals.expected_output: A whole-workspace request that lands in console but crosses into decorate's territory. Wires and verifies panes in console, but hands off to tmux-design:decorate BEFORE writing any chrome: does not hand-author `status-*` / `window-status-*` / `pane-border-*` as raw `colour###` or hex literals, and does not bake a color into a `#()` status-helper script. Gets the theme from decorate (which asks whether the terminal is light or dark, and matches an already-themed sibling session by naming the closest bundled theme rather than copying its numbers) and sets TMUX_DESIGN_THEME so panes and chrome agree. Notes that tmux_theme.sh emits global `set -g` options, which restyles every session on the server.

evals.prompt: Add a triggers pane to the right-hand column of my running monitor window — split it off the strategy pane.
evals.expected_output: Splits with tmux split-window, then recognizes that the split took its rows from the strategy sibling and that tmux rebalances nothing: resizes the column explicitly (tmux resize-pane -y, or select-layout) instead of keeping the accidental ratio, and persists it in the WINDOW's options: (main-pane-height/main-pane-width) — not a per-pane size: key, which tmuxp has no such thing. Runs the verify loop on the new pane AND captures the shrunken sibling (verify-loop step 5), since a content-fit renderer truncates rather than scrolls and a halved sibling renders a clean-looking frame with its bottom rows missing. New wrapper is checked against rule 2's flags rather than copied wholesale from a sibling watch-* script, so -w/--unfold is present.

evals.prompt: I tweaked my portfolio renderer — make sure it still fits the pane before I ship it.
evals.expected_output: Runs the bundled `scripts/check_cols.py` over the RENDERER'S STDOUT at several widths (e.g. `TMUX_PANE_WIDTH=$w <renderer> | python3 "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/check_cols.py" "$w" --reserve 1`) rather than hand-rolling an `awk length()` / `len()` / strip-SGR-and-count check — the point being that display width is measured with the same `vlen()` the renderer pads with, so the check and the renderer cannot disagree. Treats silence AND a zero exit as the pass. Does not false-alarm on a row containing an OSC-8 hyperlinked cell or a ZWJ emoji (an SGR-only strip measures a 10-column linked cell at 43). Does not pipe a `capture-pane` capture into it — without -J a capture is already hard-wrapped at pane width, so every line fits by construction and the check cannot fail.
